title: Cuba's Grid Collapses Twice in 24 Hours — Sixth Nationwide Blackout of 2026
detail: Cuba's national power grid collapsed late on August 2, 2026, and after partial restoration overnight, a fresh electrical oscillation triggered a second collapse on August 3 — the sixth island-wide blackout of the year, again cutting power to roughly 10 million people. Cuban state television news director Lázaro Manuel Alonso said 'despite the progress made today, an [electric] oscillation triggered the collapse.' The repeated failures stem from chronic fuel shortages, aging thermoelectric plants, and damaged infrastructure, worsened by the US oil blockade (EO 14380) and the halt of Venezuelan and Mexican oil shipments to the island since Maduro's January 2026 capture.

title: PANAMAX 2026: 21 Nations, 1,700 Troops Begin Panama Canal Security Exercises
detail: PANAMAX 2026, an 11-day multinational military exercise, began August 3, 2026, bringing roughly 1,700 uniformed personnel from 21 countries — including the US, Argentina, Colombia, Ecuador, Guatemala, Honduras, Peru, Brazil, Chile, Mexico, Paraguay, and several European and Caribbean states — to Panama for simultaneous maritime, land, and air drills focused on 'protecting the strategic shipping route and critical infrastructure' of the Panama Canal, which handles 3–5% of global trade. Panama's government barred any permanent foreign bases or live-fire drills, with all foreign personnel scheduled to depart by mid-August. The exercise follows a July 13–18 US-Panama drill (PANAMAX-Alpha Phase I) and an agreement letting US forces operate from three former US bases, amid mounting US concern over Chinese infrastructure investment near the canal.
